children: faces mounting competitive pressure and potential financial risks from its growing investment commitments, according to Seaport Research, which maintained its Sell rating on the chipmaker and a $180 price target.

Analyst Jay Goldberg said Nvidia's financing arrangements may reflect rising pressure from rivals. He also questioned whether the company's efforts to support customers and secure supplies could create competing demands on its financial resources.

Nvidia added roughly $250 billion in commitments during its latest quarter, according to Goldberg. Those obligations include spending to secure components and support data center construction, tying the company more closely to the expansion of AI infrastructure.

Goldberg also highlighted a separate financing initiative involving Nvidia, six private equity firms and banks. The proposed platform could provide about $500 billion in funding, with the possibility of reaching $1 trillion. Nvidia would not bear the entire obligation, but the analyst views its role as central to the arrangement.

The concern is that financing structures built to accelerate growth could magnify losses if demand for computing capacity weakens. Goldberg warned that infrastructure providers reliant on Nvidia's support could face pressure during a downturn, potentially adding strain when the chipmaker's own sales and cash flow soften.

title: Seaport Research Issues Stark Nvidia Warning on Nvidia Stock
